id.description: kebab-case id naming the METHOD (e.g. "competitive-teardown"), never the run, its id, or its subject

title.description: Short human name for the method (e.g. "Competitive teardown")

domain.description: One-or-two word category the method belongs to (e.g. "research", "ui-design", "data-migration")

instruction.description: The complete, standalone instruction a future agent receives when this skill is invoked. Written as durable method guidance for a DIFFERENT subject — no references to this run, its inputs, or its results.

doc.description: Fuller markdown reference for the method: steps, decision points, quality bar, and common failure modes. Loaded into the session as a context file when the skill is used.

tags.description: Lowercase retrieval tags for this method

confidence.description: 0..1 — how confident you are that this is a genuinely reusable method rather than a one-off description of this run

rationale.description: What in the run's nodes and gate verdicts evidences this method, and why it generalizes beyond this run's subject

evidence.description: The 2-3 most load-bearing excerpts from the run — the lines that made you name this method. Each must be VERBATIM from the node shown, because a reader will open the node and check it.

runId.description: The sub-run id shown on that node, or "" when the node belongs to the run being extracted from

nodeId.description: The node id this excerpt comes from, copied exactly from the run description

quote.description: Verbatim excerpt from that node's output or log tail, at most 300 characters. No paraphrase.
